# Aim 
Determine the Excision and reintegration efficiency of Sleeping Beauty transposons containing the same insert from different genomic loci. 

# Experimental setup
Clonal cell lines containing the SB cassette at different precise genomic locations were subject to SB mediated hopping by transfecting the cells with the SB transposase. Single cell clones were isolated from the hopped population and screened for evidence of hopping by PCR. Clones that showed indication of hopping were selected and subject to Tn5-based mapping. 

Here is the selection and analysis of excised and reintegrated clones from Figure 1C. 

# Experiments
E1682 - mapping of clones for Fzd5, Tdgf1, Nanog
E1792 - mapping of clones for T3, T48, T201, F108, N31, N37
E1828 - mapping of clones for T3, T48, T201


##NOTE
clone T201 has probably a second LP (30Mb) away, which causes weird distributions. 
Therefore filter it out.

# E1682
```{r}
clones_E1682 = clones_int_fig1 %>% filter(experiment == "E1682")

#Determine read cutoff for clones
clone_summary <- clones_E1682 %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(
    total_reads_sample = sum(read_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    fract_reads_sample = read_count / total_reads_sample
  ) %>%
  arrange(sample, desc(read_count)) %>%
  mutate(rank_in_sample = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r}
# choose thresholds
min_reads <- 3
min_fraction <- 0.2  

reliable_integrations <- clone_summary %>%
  filter(read_count >= min_reads, fract_reads_sample >= min_fraction)

# number of clones with >=1 reliable integration
n_clones_with_reliable <- reliable_integrations %>%
  summarise(n_clones = n_distinct(sample))

# per Launch site
clones_per_LS <- reliable_integrations %>%
  distinct(sample, launch_site) %>%
  dplyr::count(launch_site, name = "n_clones_with_reliable_integration")

# how many reliable integrations per clone
integrations_per_clone <- reliable_integrations %>%
  dplyr::count(sample, name = "n_reliable_integrations")

clone_class_summary <- integrations_per_clone %>%
  dplyr::count(n_reliable_integrations, name = "n_clones")

# outputs
n_clones_with_reliable
clones_per_LS
integrations_per_clone
clone_class_summary

```
**Conclusion:**
I filtered each clone to have at least 3 reads per putative integration side and that the integration should represent at least 20% of the total reads. 
By applying this filters, we find 
30 int --> Fzd5
33 int --> Nanog
48 int --> Tdgf1

## Check Tdgf1 contamination
```{r}
# Check if integtations that have the contamination also have another integration
reliable_integrations %>% filter(launch_site == "Tdgf1") %>% group_by(sample, chr) %>% summarise(count = n())

#which samples have integratios in different chr?
reliable_integrations %>% filter(launch_site == "Tdgf1") %>% group_by(sample, chr) %>% summarise(count = n()) %>% group_by(sample) %>% summarise(nr = n()) %>% arrange(desc(nr))

Tdgf1_cont_samples_with_second_int = reliable_integrations %>% 
  filter(launch_site == "Tdgf1") %>% 
  group_by(sample, chr) %>% 
  summarise(count = n()) %>% 
  group_by(sample) %>% 
  summarise(nr = n()) %>% 
  filter(nr >1) %>% 
  dplyr::pull(sample)


#Investigate suspicious samples
#reliable_integrations %>% filter(sample %in% Tdgf1_cont_samples_with_second_int) %>% View()

# New reliable integration tibble
# - filter out Tdgf1 clones that have contamination

clone_Tdgf1_cont = reliable_integrations %>% filter(launch_site == "Tdgf1" & chr == "chr1" & start == "79293540") %>% pull(sample)
clone_Tdgf1_cont_exclude =  setdiff(clone_Tdgf1_cont, Tdgf1_cont_samples_with_second_int)

#Filter out Tdgf1 clones that are contaminations
reliable_integrations_1 = reliable_integrations %>%
  filter(!sample %in% clone_Tdgf1_cont_exclude)

clones_per_LP_1 =
  reliable_integrations_1 %>% 
  distinct(sample, launch_site) %>%
  dplyr::count(launch_site, name = "n_clones_with_reliable_integration")

clones_per_LP_1
```
**Conclusion:** 
Clones "Tdgf1_clone_114" "Tdgf1_clone_135" "Tdgf1_clone_177" "Tdgf1_clone_201" "Tdgf1_clone_33" have a contaminating integration from the Fzd5_F108 LP in them but also a second integration that is reasonable. Therefore i believe them to be real. 

Fzd5 - 30
Nanog - 33
Tdgf1 - 34

clones_E1792 = clones_int_fig1 %>% filter(experiment == "E1792")

## Quality control
```{r}
# How many clones do we have per launch pad
clones_E1792 %>% 
  group_by(launch_site) %>%
  distinct(sample) %>%
  dplyr::count()

# How many do have reliable integrations?
clone_summary_E1792 <- clones_E1792 %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(
    total_reads_sample = sum(read_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    fract_reads_sample = read_count / total_reads_sample
  ) %>%
  arrange(sample, desc(read_count)) %>%
  mutate(rank_in_sample = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# Select the top two ranked ones
clone_summary_E1792 %>% 
  filter(rank_in_sample <= 2) %>%
  group_by(sample, launch_site) %>%
  dplyr::count(sample)

clone_summary_E1792 %>% 
  filter(rank_in_sample <= 2) %>%
  distinct(sample, launch_site) %>%
  dplyr::count(launch_site, name = "n_samples")


#Cutoff - each integration requires at least 10 reads
clone_summary_E1792 %>%
  filter(read_count >= 10) %>%
  group_by(launch_site) %>%
  summarize(count = n())

# Filter 
clone_summary_E1792_filtered = 
clone_summary_E1792  %>%
  filter(read_count >= 10) 
```
**Conclusion:**
In this samples there is a lot of background noise in there, I figured filtering for 10 reads per integration should give a robust cutoff. 
T48 --> 2 clones
T3 --> none left (all ints had very low read counts)

# Plot clones
I collected the numbers of total clones, excised_&_reintegrated and excised_with_no_detectable_reintegration in excel and exported them as a tsv file to plot them here. 

```{r}
tib_eff_clones_combined = read_tsv("/DATA/usr/m.eder/projects/Method_paper/Lise_hop_ReIntegrate_clone_estimation/me20260409_Clones_Lise_LD20260224.tsv")

#Filter out clone T201, has two integrations
tib_eff_clones_combined = tib_eff_clones_combined %>% 
  filter(locus != "T201")
```


## Add count clone count to each categroy
```{r}
plot_df <- tib_eff_clones_combined %>%
  mutate(hop_frac = hopped_out_clones / total_clones,
         reintegration_frac = clones_with_int / tagmented_clones,
         combined_frac = hop_frac * reintegration_frac,
         
         fract_no_excision_fraction = 1 - hop_frac,
         fract_exc_not_int_fraction = hop_frac * (1 - reintegration_frac),
         fract_exc_int_fraction = combined_frac,
         
         fract_no_excision_count = total_clones - hopped_out_clones,
         fract_exc_int_count = clones_with_int,
         fract_exc_not_int_count = tagmented_clones - clones_with_int) %>%
  select(locus,
         fract_no_excision_fraction, fract_exc_not_int_fraction, fract_exc_int_fraction,
         fract_no_excision_count, fract_exc_not_int_count, fract_exc_int_count) %>%
  
  pivot_longer(cols = -locus,
    # We split column names into TWO parts:
    # 1) category  → fract_exc_int / fract_exc_not_int / fract_no_excision
    # 2) .value    → tells pivot_longer which output column to fill
    #                ("fraction" or "count")
    names_to = c("category", ".value"),

    # Regex that splits column names like:
    # "fract_exc_int_fraction" → ("fract_exc_int", "fraction")
    # "fract_exc_int_count"    → ("fract_exc_int", "count")
    #
    # Explanation of pattern:
    # ^(.*)_(fraction|count)$
    #  ^        start of string
    #  (.*)     capture EVERYTHING before last "_"
    #           → this becomes "category"
    #  _        literal underscore
    #  (fraction|count)
    #           match either "fraction" or "count"
    #           → this becomes ".value"
    #  $        end of string
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(fraction|count)$") %>%
  mutate(category = factor(category, levels = c("fract_exc_int", "fract_exc_not_int", "fract_no_excision"),
                           labels = c("Excised + reintegrated",
                                      "Excised, no detectable reintegration",
                                      "No excision")))



#order based on Hopped + reintegrated number
locus_order <- plot_df %>%
  filter(category == "No excision") %>%
  arrange(fraction) %>%
  pull(locus)


# Plot
plot_df %>% 
mutate(locus = factor(locus, levels = locus_order)) %>% #order based on locus
ggplot(aes(x = locus, y = fraction, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::percent(fraction, accuracy = 1)),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Excised + reintegrated" = "#1B9E77",
      "Excised, no detectable reintegration" = "#E6AB02",
      "No excision" = "#D9D9D9")) +
  labs(
    x = "Locus",
    y = "Fraction of clones",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.border = element_blank()) +
  ggtitle("Hopping and re-integration efficiency based on clones")
```



## Plot including number of clones
```{r}
# Plot with clone numbers in it
plot_df %>%
mutate(locus = factor(locus, levels = locus_order),
       category = factor(category, levels = c("Excised + reintegrated", 
                                              "Excised, no detectable reintegration", 
                                              "No excision"))) %>% #order based on locus
ggplot(aes(x = locus, y = fraction, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(

    ) +

  labs(
    x = "Locus",
    y = "Fraction of clones",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.border = element_blank()) +
  ggtitle("Excision and re-integration efficiency")
```

Calculate equivalent to 'transposed fraction' (for comparison to the pool-based estimates).
Transposed fraction is excised_reintegrated/(excised_reintegrated + no_excision)
Do this calculation based on the fractions, because those represent the whole experiment (counts are a bit off because not all excised clones were actually tagmented). 

```{r}
plot_df %>%
  dplyr::select(-count) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = category,
              values_from = fraction) %>%
  mutate(transposed_fraction = `Excised + reintegrated`/(`Excised + reintegrated`+`No excision`)) %>%
  relocate(locus, transposed_fraction)

```
